---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support or product-feasibility decisions, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iPhone hardware with Camera Control where available. Proposal uses the physical control to switch accounts, opens a crowded nested settings list during capture and gives no selected-exposure feedback. The same scanner also runs on older iPhones.

# Apple HIG: Map user actions to input and alternatives

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the action and available hardware/input context, then enter the keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controller, Pencil, Crown or sensor procedure.
2. Preserve reserved system gestures and familiar input meanings. Separate targeting, focus, selection and activation; define feedback and reachable alternatives for the actions people must complete.
3. Account for comfort, precision, fatigue and switching between available inputs. Custom inputs should not remove an accessible route to an essential action.
4. Deliver an action-to-input mapping, focus/selection states and observable verification scenarios. Keep code/static observations separate from physical comfort, eye/hand and hardware checks.

## Enter the topic procedure

inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make

name: apple-hig-camera-control
description: Use when designing or reviewing iPhone Camera Control overlay functions, slider or picker choices, capture-mode availability, or locked capture entry.
---

# Make hardware adjustments predictable during capture

Read [Camera Control](../../references/camera-control.md). Inspect capture modes, existing controls, value models, viewfinder layout, and supported devices. The source describes iPhone 16/16 Pro and excludes other platforms; verify current hardware/API availability when implementing beyond that snapshot. Choose design, review, or adaptation mode and retain the existing capture stack.

Inventory the fixed control set. Use sliders for ranges and pickers for discrete choices; enable/disable controls by capture mode rather than dynamically adding/removing them. Put common functions near the middle and rare ones at the ends, accounting for the system remembering the last-used control.

Give each function a short name and an available SF Symbol representing function rather than live state; custom symbols are unsupported here. Expose meaningful units/localized values and useful prominent range values so sliding can settle precisely. Reserve overlay/label space beside the hardware control in portrait and landscape, allowing Dynamic Type enlargement. Hide duplicate app controls while the overlay is present without hiding unrelated needed information. Consider the locked camera capture extension for relevant system entrypoints.

**Before → decision → after:** A camera app adds/removes white-balance choices whenever modes change and uses a custom icon whose shape varies with temperature. Decision: the hardware overlay needs a stable function set and function identity. After, white balance remains in its fixed position but is disabled in unsupported modes, uses an available function symbol, and displays a localized temperature value while duplicate onscreen controls recede during adjustment.

Deliver the fixed function inventory, slider/picker/value contract, and overlay layouts or implementation. Fail if a remembered control disappears unexpectedly, labels overlap essential capture content, or a slider provides no usable value feedback. Static review cannot verify light-press/double-press/sliding ergonomics or lock-screen launch; list actual supported-device checks separately.

Use [SF Symbols](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-sf-symbols/SKILL.md) for available symbol configuration and [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md) for adaptive overlay space.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.
---

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

# Camera Control Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. The source describes Camera Control on iPhone 16 and 16 Pro. A light press opens a bezel-adjacent overlay, a light double press reveals controls, and sliding adjusts the selected control. ## Anatomy Use sliders for a continuous/value range and pickers for discrete choices. System zoom and exposure controls can accompany custom controls in the overlay. ## Best practices - Represent each function with an available SF Symbol; custom symbols are unsupported and the symbol represents function rather than live state. - Keep names short because Dynamic Type can enlarge labels over the viewfinder. Include units such as EV/% or a useful localized value string for sliders, and declare frequently used or regularly spaced prominent values for easier settling. - Leave overlay/label space next to the hardware control in portrait and landscape. Maximize the viewfinder, allowing the overlay over it, and hide duplicate app controls while the overlay is present. - Enable/disable the fixed set of controls according to capture mode; controls cannot be added/removed at runtime. - Put common controls near the middle and rare ones at either end. The system remembers the last control when reopening. - Provide a locked camera capture extension so people can launch the camera experience from lock screen, Home Screen, and other apps. ## Platform considerations The source marks Camera Control unsupported outside iOS. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2024.

name: apple-hig-layout
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting layout hierarchy, safe areas, size classes, resizable windows, enlarged text, or platform-specific spacing.
---

# Preserve relationships while available space changes

Read [Layout](../../references/layout.md). Inspect content priority, navigation, controls, supported environments, constraints, and current implementation. Identify design/review/adaptation mode and keep the existing layout system. Record actual available space and text/localization conditions; device names alone are insufficient evidence for a breakpoint.

Start with relationships: align peers, group related items, indent subordinates, and reveal secondary choices progressively. Place important content toward the leading/top region in the locale's reading order. Separate backgrounds that can extend beneath bars from important content/actions that must respect safe regions.

Choose adaptations from available width/height and environmental values, not a phone/tablet or portrait/landscape guess. Preserve selection, content, functionality, and idiom when columns collapse, actions overflow, or horizontal rows stack for larger text. Test the smallest and largest useful layouts first, then intermediate resizing, longer localization, direction changes, and display accommodations. Crop decorative backgrounds without distorting aspect ratio or hiding essential imagery.

Apply platform conditions deliberately: Mac essential controls cannot depend on a bottom edge that may be offscreen; TV content needs the guide's overscan insets and focus-expansion room; Watch normally needs very few side-by-side actions. visionOS windows/volumes should resize, use meaningful bounds, and avoid inline 3D crowding controls; use separate volumes for model-centric work. Read numeric platform specifications from the guide rather than generalizing one platform's spacing.

**Before → decision → after:** A reading list positions Delete at a fixed bottom coordinate and fixes each row to one line. Decision: resized windows and enlarged titles need flow-based layout. After, row height/wrapping adapt, secondary actions remain reachable through contextual overflow, and the selected article persists when the sidebar collapses.

Deliver corrected layouts/constraints or implementation plus an environment matrix. Fail if a required action disappears, related items detach, content overlaps hardware/bars, or resizing changes the task's meaning. Report tested dimensions/settings; static or Linux checks cannot establish native safe-area/focus behavior absent supported execution.

Use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md) for text behavior, [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for direction, and [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for 3D position/scale.

name: apple-hig-sf-symbols
description: Use when selecting or configuring SF Symbols, rendering modes, weights, variants, variable color, animations, custom symbols, or symbol availability.
---

# Configure the symbol's meaning before its decoration

Read [SF Symbols](../../references/sf-symbols.md). Inspect the intended action/state, neighboring type, background, deployment OS, and existing glyph implementation. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested symbol assignment/configuration or custom-symbol specification within the existing stack. Check individual symbol/feature availability and licensing; library symbols cannot become product trademarks or app icons.

Select the semantic variant before styling: outline for ordinary text-adjacent controls, fill for supported emphasis/selection, enclosure for small-size clarity, or slash for negation. Let standard views choose variants when appropriate. Match symbol weight to adjacent text, then use scale to adjust emphasis without mismatching stroke weight.

Choose rendering by information. Monochrome suits one tint; hierarchical communicates layer importance; palette assigns intentional semantic colors; multicolor preserves intrinsic meaning. Variable color represents a quantity by activating layers and should exclude stable parts. It is not a substitute for hierarchy. Use adaptive colors and test the actual size/background rather than trusting automatic rendering.

If animating, select an effect whose meaning matches the event: a once-only bounce for feedback differs from ongoing pulse/breathe activity or a replacement state transition. Avoid simultaneous effects that conflict. For custom art, start from an appropriate template, preserve optical alignment, annotate whole layers/erase behavior and animation groups, and test presets. Do not modify restricted Apple product/feature symbols.

**Before → decision → after:** A fan control bounces forever and changes the whole icon's tint to show speed. Decision: rotation conveys operation while variable layers can convey quantity; the housing stays stable. After, an appropriate supported symbol configuration separates operating feedback from a labeled speed value, respects motion preferences, and keeps its housing readable.

Deliver names, supported variants/modes, state mapping, and fallback choices or implementation. Fail if a symbol is unavailable on the deployment OS, rendering erases a meaningful layer, or animation implies work after it stopped. Native/custom-symbol animation and localized variants require actual supported previews; static inspection cannot verify them.

Use [Icons](../apple-hig-icons/SKILL.md) when selecting a metaphor, [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md) for interaction timing, or [Right to left](../apple-hig-right-to-left/SKILL.md) for directional semantics.

# Designing for iOS Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. An iPhone experience must work both during brief checks on the move and through extended games, browsing, or media sessions. People switch among apps frequently. ## Best practices - Design for a medium-sized, dense display viewed at roughly 1–2 feet, usually held in one or both hands. Accommodate portrait and landscape use. - Keep primary content and actions clear, with secondary operations reachable through a small number of interactions rather than many simultaneous controls. - Support touch gestures, onscreen keyboards, and voice; use motion sensors, nearby spatial interactions, or personal information only where they improve the task. - Put frequent touch controls within comfortable reach, commonly the middle or lower display. Preserve swipe-back navigation and list-row gestures. - Adapt to orientation, Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type without breaking context. - With permission, use platform data and services to reduce typing: location, biometric authentication, and payments are examples. - Integrate appropriate system entry points: widgets, Home Screen quick actions, Spotlight search, Shortcuts, and activity views. Their familiar behavior helps people act outside the main app. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here.

item.text: The local guidance calls for a fixed set of capture controls, with slider values shown in meaningful units and space reserved beside the hardware control. I’ll remove account switching and nested settings from Camera Control, define Exposure and Zoom adjustments, and keep equivalent touch actions for older iPhones.

item.aggregated_output: # Layout Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Use predictable relationships among content and controls while adapting to the actual available space. ## Visual hierarchy Prioritize important content toward the top and leading edge in reading order. Use system components for RTL adaptation. Align related items, indent subordinate items, and group relationships with space, containers, or separators. Reveal secondary choices progressively through disclosure, menus, nested views, or scrollable media sections. Distinguish navigation/controls with Liquid Glass and scroll-edge treatments; extend full-window backgrounds under bars and sidebars. A background extension effect can mirror and blur imagery under adjacent components instead of hiding essential original art. ## Adaptability Handle size classes, display sizes, orientation/aspect ratio, Dynamic Island, external displays, Display Zoom, resizable windows, text changes, localized length/direction/fonts, and date/number formats. Use SwiftUI or Auto Layout, safe areas, margins, and layout modifiers. Orientation-locked games must still resize. With large text, stack horizontal content, increase row height, and allow wrapping. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can supply Dynamic Type in games. Preview smallest/largest layouts first, then multiple devices, localizations, sizes, iPad resizing, and iPhone Mirroring. Scale backgrounds to fill without distorting aspect ratio; extreme wide/short or narrow/tall windows may crop much more than standard displays. ### Size classes Each axis is compact or regular, describing available width or height rather than device type or orientation. All four combinations can occur as apps resize, multitask, or mirror. Base layout on these environmental values, not idiom/orientation guesses. Preserve functionality across classes while changing how much is exposed, such as sidebar versus tabs or visible actions versus overflow. The platform idiom remains the same during resizing, so preserve its familiar character. ## Guides and safe areas Layout guides supply rectangular regions for alignment, spacing, margins, and readable text widths; custom guides can add app-specific structure. Safe areas exclude edge obstructions such as camera hardware, status bars, tab bars, and toolbars. Keep important content and controls within the appropriate safe regions. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS rules are listed. ### macOS Do not rely on the bottom of a window for essential controls because it may sit below the physical display. Avoid placing content behind the top camera housing. ### tvOS Inset primary content 60 pt vertically and 80 pt horizontally to withstand TV overscan/settings. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Six-column grid Unfocused item width: 260 pt. Horizontal gap: 40 pt. Minimum vertical gap: 100 pt. #### Seven-column grid Unfocused item width: 217 pt. Monochrome gives all layers one tint with transparent cutouts. Hierarchical varies one tint’s opacity by layer importance. Palette assigns multiple colors; with two colors for three hierarchy levels, secondary and tertiary share a color. Multicolor uses intrinsic meaning-bearing colors and may allow tinting some layers. Use system colors for appearance/accessibility adaptation. Even automatic mode needs legibility checks at actual sizes and backgrounds. ## Gradients SF Symbols 7 adds single-source-color linear gradients across rendering modes, custom/system colors, and custom symbols. Exclude stable parts, such as a speaker body, from the changing layers. Small, medium (default), and large scales are relative to cap height. All library symbols and custom symbols can animate across modes, weights, and scales, but custom art needs testing. ## Custom symbols Export a similar template and edit vectors while matching detail, optical weight, alignment, position, and perspective. # Revised document-scanner interaction specification

## Scope and decisions

This is a framework-agnostic design contract for the scanner described in "'`interface.md`. The supplied brief states that Camera Control switches accounts, opens a crowded nested settings list during capture, and provides no selected-exposure feedback. It also requires older-iPhone support. No implementation or screenshots were supplied.

1. **Camera Control adjusts capture only.** Remove account switching and general settings from its functions. Keep account selection outside the active capture flow: Scan home → Account → select account → return to Scan home. An active scan retains its destination account; changing accounts applies to a new scan. Settings are available from Scan home. This is a product decision applying the capture-focused overlay model and iOS hierarchy guidance, rather than a quoted Apple prohibition on accounts. [Camera Control — Anatomy and Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control#Anatomy), [Designing for iOS — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios#Best-practices).
2. **Use a small, fixed inventory:** Zoom, Exposure, in that order throughout the capture session. Both are frequent scan adjustments; with two entries neither can uniquely occupy the middle. Do not add low-value controls just to create a middle position. If a future inventory grows, place frequent functions centrally and rare ones at the ends. Disable unavailable functions in place; never insert or remove entries on a mode change. Respect the system'"'s remembered function. [Camera Control — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control#Best-practices).
3. **Use system Zoom and Exposure controls when the eventual integration supports them.** Otherwise adapt the same value contracts below without inventing SDK calls or custom hardware gestures. Camera Control is an enhancement; every scan action remains available by touch on older phones. The local source names iPhone 16 and 16 Pro and excludes non-iOS platforms; it does not establish support for every later iPhone. Integration must use actual capability checks, not a model-name inference. [Camera Control — Anatomy and Platform considerations](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control#Platform-considerations).

## Function and value contract

Ranges below are product targets, not HIG-mandated limits. Intersect them with actual camera capabilities before registering the fixed inventory; retain the inventory identities afterward. Use actual applied values as the single source for both touch and hardware presentations.

| Function | Kind and initial value | Range and prominent values | Name and symbol |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom | Slider; 1× if supported, otherwise nearest supported value | Target 1×–3×, bounded by supported scan-camera range; prominent 1×, 2×, 3× where supported | “Zoom”; use system Zoom identity; custom-adapter candidate "'`plus.magnifyingglass` |
| Exposure | Slider for exposure compensation; 0 EV if supported | Target −2 to +2 EV, intersected with supported bounds; prominent whole EV values and endpoints; preserve finer supported adjustments | “Exposure”; use system Exposure identity; custom-adapter candidate `plusminus.circle` |

Exposure readout example: **Exposure +0.7 EV**; neutral: **Exposure 0 EV**. Zoom example: **Zoom 1.5×**. Localize number formatting, names, and value strings. Show units on every selected value. Report applied camera values, including quantization or clamping, rather than a requested value the camera rejected. Markers help settling without forcing whole-EV steps. If an adjustment fails, retain the last applied value and show “Adjustment unavailable.” Disable the control with an explanation if its range cannot vary.

For custom-adapter candidates, verify the exact SF Symbol against the deployment environment before release; these names are proposals, not availability evidence. Use a verified library alternative for the same function if necessary, never custom artwork in this overlay. Match neighboring text weight, use a static monochrome function symbol, and do not change its identity with slider value. A system-provided control supplies its own identity. These contracts apply the source'"'s short-label, value/unit, prominent-value, and library-symbol guidance. [Camera Control — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control#Best-practices), [SF Symbols — Weights and scales](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/sf-symbols#Weights-and-scales).

No discrete setting is needed in this minimal inventory. If a future capture function offers enumerated choices, use a picker rather than a continuous slider; it still requires a fixed inventory revision outside the active session.

## Interaction and state model

"'`phase = home | live | capturing | review | suspended`; `overlay = closed | adjusting | choosing`. Maintain `pages`, `scanAccount`, `appliedValues`, and platform-managed remembered function independently of overlay visibility.

| Event and precondition | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Open scanner | Enter live preview after camera readiness; show touch Capture, Zoom and Exposure controls, page count and destination account. Capture is disabled until ready. |
| Light press in live preview | Request the system'"'s adjustment overlay for its remembered function. Show its name, current value and units immediately. Do not reset the remembered function each time. |
| Light double press | Reveal the flat fixed function selector; no nested app settings or account menu. |
| Select a function, then slide | Use system selection/adjustment behavior; change only the selected enabled function. Apply and display the accepted value in the live preview. Selecting a disabled function cannot change values; show the unavailable reason. |
| Dismiss overlay through system behavior | Restore duplicate touch controls with the same values; retain selected function and scan state. Do not invent a dismissal timeout or repurpose a reserved gesture. |
| Touch Zoom or Exposure | Open a single-level equivalent adjustment surface bound to the same values. Touch Capture remains available. |
| Capture action while live and ready | Capture one page through the existing scanner capture path; reject duplicate in-flight requests; retain account and prior pages. On success increment count and return to live preview. On failure keep existing pages and show a retryable status. |
| Review pages | Close overlay; disable capture adjustments in place for review mode; show captured pages. Returning to live restores values, function identity and enabled state. |
| Background/interruption | Close overlay, suspend capture requests, preserve pages, account and values. On return reestablish camera readiness, reconcile values to supported bounds, and display applied values before enabling capture. |

A physical full press may invoke the same capture action if the verified platform integration offers that event. This is a proposed mapping requiring implementation/device verification; the supplied local article explicitly documents light press, light double press and sliding, but does not specify full-press capture dispatch. Never emulate hardware press thresholds or override system launch/gesture meanings. If full-press dispatch is unavailable, touch Capture still completes scanning.

Pseudocode describes application events, not Apple APIs:

"'```text
onAdjustment(function, requested):
    require phase == live and cameraReady and enabled[function]
    accepted = cameraAdapter.apply(function, bound(requested))
    if accepted.success:
        appliedValues[function] = accepted.actualValue
    else:
        showStatus("Adjustment unavailable")
    refreshHardwareAndTouchValues(appliedValues)

onCaptureRequested():
    if phase != live or not cameraReady: return
    phase = capturing  // serialize auto, touch, and supported hardware triggers
    capturePageIntoCurrentScan(scanAccount)
    // success: append once; failure: retain pages and offer retry
    phase = live when cameraReady
```

The source recommends a locked camera capture extension. Include it as a separate integration requirement for supported system entrypoints; it is not supplied by this specification. Its destination should be a fresh scanner capture session, not accounts or settings. Authentication, saved-document access and handoff need a separate defined contract before shipping locked capture. No lock-screen launch is claimed here. [Camera Control — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control#Best-practices).

## Overlay and fallback layout

In portrait and landscape, reserve room along the physical Camera Control edge for the system overlay and enlarged name/value labels. Maximize the preview beneath that overlay; keep page count, capture status and destination account outside its label footprint. Place document framing guidance in the remaining clear preview area; reflow guidance when the overlay opens. Do not place an essential action in that reserved edge area.

While the hardware overlay is visible, hide only the duplicate touch Zoom and Exposure controls. Keep Capture, page count and review access available. Restore duplicate controls on dismissal. On older phones, always show those touch controls; do not leave an empty hardware-overlay strip or display hardware-only instructions.

Use available bounds and safe regions to position controls, rather than hard-coded device coordinates. At enlarged text sizes, wrap names/values and stack app controls as needed; keep the selected value readable without covering Capture or page status. Preserve selected values and pages across rotation. Exact overlay extents require real integration measurements; this document does not invent pixel bounds. [Camera Control — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/camera-control#Best-practices), [Layout — Adaptability and Guides and safe areas](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout#Adaptability).

## Worked before/after

**Before (supplied):** During a document scan, Camera Control changes accounts and opens nested settings; the selected exposure has no feedback. The brief does not establish the exact gesture sequence or slider range.

**After (illustrative trace):** A user starts a scan for Work. In live preview, light press opens remembered Exposure with “Exposure 0 EV.” Sliding requests +0.7 EV; assuming the camera accepts it, the preview and label update to “Exposure +0.7 EV.” Duplicate touch exposure/zoom controls recede, while Capture and page count remain visible. The user captures using touch Capture (or verified full-press integration), adding page 1 to Work. Dismissing and reopening the overlay retains Exposure and +0.7 EV. Light double press reveals only Zoom and Exposure. Account selection remains on Scan home and cannot silently redirect this scan. On an older iPhone the user performs the same exposure adjustment with the touch control and captures into Work.

## Acceptance checks and evidence status

**Passed — document inspection only:** Read the installed root, Inputs and Getting started families, iOS and Camera Control procedures, then their source guides; followed Camera Control'"'s routed Foundations family, Layout and SF Symbols procedures and guides. The revised contract contains a fixed inventory, value feedback, explicit mode availability, remembered selection, orientation behavior and older-phone fallback. These are specification checks, not executed behavior.

**Failed — supplied proposal against the revised contract:** Account switching occupies the capture input; a crowded nested settings list replaces a flat capture selector; exposure lacks selected-value feedback. Evidence is the text of "'`interface.md`, not an observed app run.

**Not executed — acceptance scenarios for implementation:**

- On a supported device, light press opens the remembered function, light double press exposes the fixed selector, and sliding changes only the selected adjustment. Verify physical comfort and system behavior separately from event simulations.
- Apply +0.7 EV, dismiss/reopen, rotate, and interrupt/resume: the applied value remains accurate and visible with units. Camera clamping and errors never leave a stale requested value on screen.
- Enter capturing/review/suspended states: unavailable functions remain registered in the same order, cannot mutate values, and return enabled when live and ready. A remembered disabled function never disappears.
- Trigger simultaneous capture sources: exactly one page is appended per accepted capture, with existing pages and destination preserved on failure.
- Inspect portrait, landscape, smallest supported usable bounds, and largest supported text settings: labels remain readable, no essential content/action overlaps the overlay, and duplicate controls return on dismissal. Record actual bounds/settings when performed.
- On an older phone or unavailable Camera Control capability, complete adjustment, capture and review through touch; no hardware-only step blocks scanning.
- Verify exact symbol availability, applied range/units, platform event support and any locked-capture launch/handoff against the eventual deployment target. No unavailable/custom overlay glyph is shipped.

## Evidence limits

Only supplied local text and installed guidance were used; no web browsing occurred. Official links above identify the cited articles, not pages fetched in this task. The local Camera Control guide is retrieved 2026-10-25 and records source revision September 9, 2024; it is a dated, independently packaged interpretation of HIG, not an SDK reference. Its iPhone 16/16 Pro description cannot certify newer hardware, exact APIs, press dispatch or symbol availability.

No device, Apple SDK, build, GUI, physical gesture, accessibility, safe-area rendering, haptic or locked-capture execution was performed. No measured layout or runtime accessibility result is asserted. Product assumptions introduced here are the two-function inventory, target ranges, account ownership rule and capture-state behavior; validate those with the existing capture stack before implementation.
EOF'
